newsitem.title: JAPAN: MITI panel calls for more financial deregulations.
newsitem.headline: MITI panel calls for more financial deregulations.

text.p: Japan should remove the barriers to entering its financial industry so that companies can raise or manage funds more smoothly and efficiently, a subcommittee under the Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI) said on Monday.
Regulations in financial service should be limited in principle to only those concerning settlement system risks and fair trade, the subcommittee for industrial finance said in a statement.

To promote competition, the current licencing system for financial service providers should be changed to a registration system in order to facilitate entry of new players into the financial industry, the subcommittee said.
"The aim of this subcommittee is to make sure that the opinions of financial service users would be heard in the on-going 'Big Bang' financial market reform debate," a MITI official told Reuters.
The subcommittee, made up of 19 members including scholars, corporate directors and think tank economists, aims to finalise its financial reform proposals by early June, he said.

The subcommittee suggested in the statement that the regulations concerning brokerage commissions on listed stocks, commodity futures and financial futures should also be scrapped, since they discourage low-cost asset management by companies and do not necessarily work to prevent unfair trade.

"It does not make any sense to delay the liberalisation of brokerage commissions when we already know that the foreign exchange law will be revised (in the fiscal year beginning in April 1998)," the MITI official said.
If Japanese institutions were unable to offer financial products at prices competitive with overseas counterparts, their clients will simply do business abroad after the forex deregulation, he said.
The subcommittee said it also discussed whether the current ban on bond and commercial paper issuance by leasing and credit firms should be lifted.
